title: Corporate Strategy Metaphors
completion_message: ¡Brillante! El lenguaje de la alta dirección está lleno de metáforas bélicas y marítimas. Expresiones como 'move the goalposts' o 'weather the storm' te dan la autoridad narrativa que se espera de un líder estratégico a nivel C2.

parts.visual:
El vocabulario estratégico en C2 utiliza metáforas profundas para describir poder, riesgo y negociación: 

1. Move the goalposts (Cambiar las reglas del juego / Cambiar los objetivos a mitad del proceso). 
Ej: We will never finish if management keeps moving the goalposts. 

2. Weather the storm (Capear el temporal / Sobrevivir a una crisis difícil). 
Ej: The company has enough reserves to weather the economic storm. 

3. An uphill battle (Una batalla cuesta arriba / Una tarea sumamente difícil). 
Ej: Launching the product now will be an uphill battle.
parts.audio: Strategic vocabulary at the C2 level uses deep metaphors to describe power, risk, and negotiation. Number 1: Move the goalposts. This means to unfairly change the rules or objectives while a process is ongoing. For example: We will never finish if management keeps moving the goalposts. Number 2: Weather the storm. This means to survive a difficult situation or crisis. For example: The company has enough reserves to weather the economic storm. Number 3: An uphill battle. This implies a very difficult struggle. For example: Launching the product now will be an uphill battle.

parts.visual:
4. Stalemate / Deadlock (Punto muerto / Estancamiento en una negociación). 
Ej: The negotiations have reached a stalemate. 

5. Concede (Conceder / Ceder en una negociación). 
Ej: We had to concede on the pricing to secure the contract. 

6. Find middle ground (Encontrar un punto intermedio / Llegar a un acuerdo mutuo). 
Ej: Both parties need to find middle ground if this merger is going to work. 

7. The elephant in the room (El elefante en la habitación / Un problema evidente que nadie quiere mencionar).
parts.audio: Number 4: Stalemate or Deadlock. This refers to a situation in which no progress can be made, especially in negotiations. For example: The negotiations have reached a stalemate. Number 5: Concede. To yield or give in during a negotiation. For example: We had to concede on the pricing to secure the contract. Number 6: Find middle ground. This means to find a compromise. For example: Both parties need to find middle ground if this merger is going to work. Number 7: The elephant in the room. This refers to an obvious problem or controversial issue that people avoid discussing.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la metáfora de estrategia corporativa correcta.

questions.question: It’s unfair that every time we reach the target, they ____ the goalposts. (Cambian los objetivos).
questions.explanation: Move the goalposts = cambiar las reglas a mitad del juego.

questions.question: Despite the severe recession, the bank managed to ____ the storm. (Capear/Sobrevivir).
questions.explanation: Weather the storm = sobrevivir a la crisis.

questions.question: Gaining market share from the current monopoly is going to be an uphill ____. (Batalla difícil).
questions.explanation: An uphill battle = una tarea ardua / cuesta arriba.

questions.question: The negotiations over the new contract have reached a ____. Neither side will compromise. (Punto muerto).
We had to ____ to their demands regarding the delivery schedule. (Ceder).
To avoid a lawsuit, both companies need to find middle ____. (Punto intermedio / Acuerdo).
questions.explanation: Find middle ground = encontrar un punto de acuerdo.

questions.question: No one wanted to talk about the massive debt; it was the ____ in the room.
questions.explanation: The elephant in the room = el problema obvio que se ignora.

questions.question: The CEO's resignation was a huge ____ blow to the company's reputation. (Golpe devastador).
They are a small startup trying to swim with the ____ in Silicon Valley. (Tiburones / Grandes empresas).
questions.explanation: Swim with the sharks = competir con los poderosos y peligrosos.

questions.question: The new legislation will definitely level the playing ____ for smaller businesses. (Igualar las condiciones).
questions.explanation: Level the playing field = hacer la competencia justa para todos.

questions.question: We are operating in unchartered ____ with this new AI technology. (Territorio desconocido).
The board decided to pull the ____ on the project after seeing the terrible sales figures. (Cancelar/Detener).
questions.explanation: Pull the plug = cancelar, desconectar un proyecto.

questions.question: We need to hit the ground ____ when the fiscal year starts. (Empezar a toda marcha).
questions.explanation: Hit the ground running = empezar rápidamente y con éxito.

questions.question: Our competitor is clearly in the driving ____ right now. (Al mando / En control).
questions.explanation: In the driving seat = tener el control de la situación.

questions.question: The new marketing strategy really missed the ____. It was a failure. (Fallar el objetivo).
questions.explanation: Miss the mark = no lograr el objetivo / ser inexacto.

questions.question: We must stay ahead of the ____ if we want to survive in tech. (Estar a la vanguardia / Adelantarse).
questions.explanation: Stay ahead of the curve = ir un paso adelante de la competencia/tendencias.

questions.question: The company is walking a tightrope between profitability and customer satisfaction. (Caminando por la cuerda floja).
questions.explanation: Walk a tightrope = estar en una situación muy delicada de equilibrio.

questions.question: The CEO decided to drop a ____ during the meeting by announcing his retirement. (Dar una noticia impactante).
questions.explanation: Drop a bombshell = dar una noticia sorprendente o chocante.

questions.question: We are currently the ____ runner in the race for the government contract. (El candidato favorito/líder).
questions.explanation: Front runner = el competidor con más posibilidades de ganar.

questions.question: Their aggressive pricing is just a race to the ____. (Carrera hacia el abismo/precios más bajos).
questions.explanation: Race to the bottom = competencia destructiva reduciendo precios/calidad.

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra que falta en la metáfora.

questions.question: ____ the goalposts. (Cambiar los objetivos con M)
____ the storm. (Sobrevivir a la crisis con W)
An uphill ____. (Batalla cuesta arriba)
Reach a ____. (Punto muerto con S)
Find middle ____. (Acuerdo intermedio con G)
The ____ in the room. (Problema ignorado)
Level the playing ____. (Igualar condiciones)
Pull the ____. (Cancelar un proyecto con P)
Hit the ground ____. (Empezar rápido y bien)
In the driving ____. (Al mando / Control)
